home.title: Back up entire disks. Restore them exactly.
home.lead: VolSave images Windows disks and volumes while Windows runs, verifies every image and restores it sector by sector – until Windows boots again.
home.ctaFine: Free and open source (GPL-3.0). Windows 10/11 and Windows PE, no installation.

features.title: Everything an image needs.
features.lead: No agent, no service, no cloud. One EXE file that backs up, verifies and restores.

items.title: While Windows runs
items.text: Backups go through the Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS). Windows keeps running and the image stays consistent.

items.title: The whole disk
items.text: Partition table, boot code and every partition in one image – for BIOS/MBR and UEFI/GPT.

items.title: Only used blocks
items.text: Free space is skipped and the rest is compressed with zstd. What Windows excludes through FilesNotToBackup stays out.

items.title: Differential images
items.text: After a full backup, store only the changes. No long chains: each differential image needs only its full backup.

items.title: Verify, don't hope
items.text: verify checks an image at any time. restore --verify reads the target back after restoring and compares it.

items.title: Runs in Windows PE
items.text: Works without installation in Windows PE. There VolSave reads volumes directly, since the installed Windows is not running.

cli.title: Made for scripts.
cli.text: Every command runs from cmd, PowerShell or Task Scheduler. VolSave writes a log next to each image and reports the result through a clear exit code.

items.title: Pick instead of type
items.text: Disks and partitions at a glance. Choose a whole disk or a single volume and back it up – optionally as a differential image that stores only what changed since the full backup.

items.title: Restore with verification
items.text: Restore disk and volume images and check the result – also without a license.

items.title: Runs everywhere
items.text: Windows 10/11 and Windows PE. The software renderer needs no graphics driver.

items.title: One file for both
items.text: Double-click volsave-pro.exe and the interface opens. Called with arguments, the same file works as a command line – with the same commands as the free volsave, for cmd, PowerShell, scripts and Task Scheduler.

items.title: Clone directly
items.text: Copy a whole disk onto another without an image in between – for example when moving to a new SSD. It reads through VSS snapshots, used blocks only, and checks the target afterwards. In the window with the Clone mode, on the command line with volsave-pro clone HD0 HD1.

items.title: Encrypted images
items.text: On request a password protects the image: AES-256-GCM, with the key derived from the password using Argon2id. That covers split images and differential images, too. Without the password an encrypted image cannot be restored – there is no back door.

items.q: What is the difference between VolSave and VolSave Pro?
a: VolSave is the free command line tool under the GPL-3.0. It backs up, verifies, restores and merges images.

VolSave Pro is a separate, commercial product with a graphical interface. It uses the same libraries and can also encrypt images with a password and clone disks directly; network targets are planned there.

items.q: Can I back up while Windows is running?
a: Yes. VolSave uses the Windows Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS). The image shows the state at the moment of the snapshot, even if you keep working.

items.q: Does VolSave work in Windows PE?
a: Yes, without installation. In Windows PE VolSave reads volumes directly without VSS, because the installed Windows is not running there. That way you can also restore the disk Windows normally boots from.

Unlocked BitLocker volumes – always the case for the running Windows – are saved decrypted through a VSS snapshot: only used blocks, compressed and consistent. The image then holds the data unencrypted, so keep it safe. A restored copy is not encrypted until you turn BitLocker on again.
With --bitlocker-raw VolSave copies such partitions as encrypted sectors instead. Locked volumes, e.g. in Windows PE without manage-bde -unlock, can only be copied that way.
VolSave Pro can also encrypt the image with its own password. The restored copy is still not encrypted with BitLocker; turn BitLocker on again afterwards.

Yes, with VolSave Pro. Choose “Encrypt” when backing up and set a password of at least 8 characters. The image and its hash list are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, with the key derived from the password using Argon2id. A differential image of an encrypted full image is always encrypted, with the full image’s password.
On the command line use --encrypt; for scripts and Task Scheduler, --password-file reads the password from a file. The password is never an argument, so it does not show up in the process list.
To restore, VolSave Pro asks for the password; no license is needed for that. Keep the password safe: without it an encrypted image cannot be restored. There is no recovery and no back door.

A differential image (--diff) stores only what changed since a full backup. It builds on that full backup's hash list. There are no incremental chains: to restore, you need only the differential image and its full backup.
volsave merge combines both into a new full image.

items.q: Can I clone to a different disk?
a: Yes. With the free VolSave you first back up the disk as an image and then restore it onto the new disk with volsave restore … HD1.

VolSave Pro also clones directly, without an image in between: in the window with the Clone mode, or with volsave-pro clone HD0 HD1. It reads like a backup, through VSS snapshots, and writes and verifies like a restore. Cloning needs a license.

Either way the clone keeps the disk ID of the original. While both disks are attached, the clone stays offline. Do not set it online there, or Windows gives it a new ID and it no longer boots. Shut down, remove the original disk and boot from the clone.
Windows 10 and 11 as well as Windows PE. Windows 10 and 11 with BIOS/MBR and with UEFI/GPT have been cloned and booted successfully, in virtual machines and on real hardware.
VolSave is in early development, but already in use. Check every important image with volsave verify and test a restore before you rely on it – as with any backup tool.
